extract:
Jarabe De Palo was a Spanish rock band from Barcelona, formed in the mid-1990s around singer, songwriter and guitarist Pau Donés. Active from 1996 until Donés's death in June 2020, the group became one of the most commercially successful acts in rock en español. Its Mediterranean blend of rock, pop, Latin rhythms and rumba catalana carried it well beyond Spain, into Latin America and especially Italy.

Donés had played in bands in Barcelona before assembling Jarabe De Palo as a vehicle for his own songs. Those songs drew on the city's rumba tradition, Caribbean and Cuban music, and straightforward guitar rock. His raspy, conversational voice and loose, swinging arrangements set the band apart from the harder-edged Spanish rock of the period. The project's debut album, La Flaca (1996), initially sold modestly. Then its title track was used in a television advertisement in 1997, and the song became a massive hit. The album went on to sell over a million copies, and "La Flaca" became a standard of Spanish-language pop-rock.

The follow-up, Depende (1998), consolidated that success. Its title song, a wry meditation on how everything is relative, became nearly as emblematic as "La Flaca." The band's popularity in Italy led to Dipende (2000), an Italian-language version, a pattern later repeated with Completo Incompleto and Bonito. De Vuelta Y Vuelta (2001) continued the band's warm, rhythm-driven style. Bonito (2003) produced one of their most-loved singles in the optimistic title track. Un metro cuadrado (2004) offered a stripped-down, intimate take on their material, and Romeo y Julieta followed as a single the same year. Adelantando (2007) and its accompanying single "Ole" showed the band still producing radio material, with "Ole" even receiving a remix treatment. Orquesta Reciclando (2009) reworked earlier songs, and "Em Sento Bé" marked an excursion into Catalan, Donés's other native language.

Within the late-1990s Spanish scene, Jarabe De Palo stood alongside acts such as Estopa, Los Rodríguez and Manolo García as part of a wave of Spanish pop-rock rooted in local tradition yet commercially broad. The band toured extensively in Latin America, where "La Flaca" and "Depende" became widely known. Its Italian releases made it one of the few Spanish rock groups with a sustained following in Italy. Critics sometimes regarded the band as lightweight, but the durability of its biggest songs and Donés's craft as a melodic writer earned it lasting respect.

Later albums included ¿Y ahora qué hacemos? (2011), Somos (2014) and the anniversary project 50 Palos (2017). Donés was diagnosed with colon cancer in 2015 and spoke openly about his illness in interviews and in a memoir. He released a final album and the single "Eso que tú me das" shortly before his death in 2020, at age 53, and his farewell interview drew wide attention in Spain. Jarabe De Palo's legacy rests on a handful of enduring songs, "La Flaca," "Depende" and "Bonito" foremost among them, and on Donés's image as a cheerful, life-affirming figure in Spanish popular music.
title: Jarabe De Palo
